nodes.description: Unnamed payable external fallback function of StaticCallProxy: decodes target, gas and value from raw calldata, forwards the remaining calldata via a low-level CALL and reverts with the returned data.
External caller of the payable fallback function; there is no access restriction, so any address can trigger the proxy and thereby cause arbitrary outbound calls.
Assembly CALL with fully calldata-controlled gas, destination and value: call(_gas,_dst,_value,0,_len,0,0). Anyone can make the contract call an arbitrary address and spend/forward its ether.
Assembly sub(calldatasize, 96) computes the payload length; if calldatasize < 96 the subtraction wraps around, giving an attacker-controlled huge length used for calldatacopy/CALL.
Local _dst = calldataload(0): attacker-supplied destination address for the forwarded CALL.
Local _gas = calldataload(32): attacker-supplied gas amount for the forwarded CALL.
Local _value = calldataload(64): attacker-supplied ether value sent with the forwarded CALL.
Local _len = sub(calldatasize, 96): length of the proxied calldata, computed from the untrusted calldata size.
Local ret: raw 256-bit result flag returned by the low-level CALL, written to memory with mstore8.
Local result_len = returndatasize(): size of the data returned by the arbitrary external call, copied to memory and returned via revert.

edges.reason: Any external address can invoke the payable fallback; msg.sender is not checked, so the proxy's capability to perform arbitrary calls is open to everyone.
The fallback unconditionally executes a low-level CALL whose target, gas and value are taken straight from untrusted calldata.
The fallback computes sub(calldatasize, 96) without checking that calldatasize is at least 96.
calldataload(0) provides the destination address _dst used by the forwarded call.
calldataload(32) provides the gas amount _gas used by the forwarded call.
calldataload(64) provides the value _value sent with the forwarded call.
_len is the result of sub(calldatasize, 96); an undersized calldata makes it wrap around to a huge value.
Attacker-controlled _dst flows into the CALL destination, allowing arbitrary external calls.
Attacker-controlled _gas flows into the CALL gas argument.
Attacker-controlled _value flows into the CALL value argument, allowing the contract's ether to be forwarded arbitrarily.
_len determines how many calldata bytes are forwarded as the call input.
The CALL result flag is stored in _ret and written to memory before reverting.
returndatasize() of the CALL provides result_len, which is copied and returned to the caller.

normalization_plan.reason: _dst is only used as the destination of the low-level CALL; it is not a meaningful independent abstraction and should be folded into the unsafe call node.
_gas is only consumed by the CALL as its gas parameter, so it can be merged into the unsafe call node.
_value is only consumed by the CALL as its value parameter; the ether-transfer risk is fully captured by the unsafe call node.
_len is the direct result of sub(calldatasize, 96) and should be represented by the arithmetic unsafe operation that produces it.
_ret simply holds the success flag returned by CALL and adds no separate semantics beyond the unsafe call itself.
result_len is the returndatasize of the same CALL; it is a direct by-product of the unsafe call and can be merged into it.
